A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same continual memorization and REMIX study. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and corresponding material can be matched despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original Llama-3-8B and Mistral-7B experiments measuring forgetting, replay, REMIX, knowledge manipulation, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds parameter-expansion comparisons, stage-2 training and test results, and a stricter entity-overlap analysis.

M1.justification: REMIX retains the same random-word and generic-data mixing procedure at either or both training stages. The added LoRA implementation is a comparator, while corrections to the displayed gradient updates do not establish a change to REMIX's training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same factoid, mathematics, coding, chat, mixing-corpus, and MMLU coverage, including familiar-fact and three-stage scenarios. The new stage-2 evaluations use existing datasets; removing the Mistral familiar-fact table does not remove that population from the retained Llama evaluation.

E2.justification: V3 Table 4 adds a parameter-expansion baseline implemented using LoRA, evaluated for KVR, PopQA, and TriviaQA against LAMA, EntityQA, and WebQA. The existing no-mixing, weight-regularization, behavior-regularization, and replay comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New Appendix B.2 evaluates stage-2 training accuracy and separate test-set accuracy on GSM8K, MATH, and APPS. B.10 adds an overlap-checking procedure restricted to selected entity types. The newly stated 2,000-example training sizes and deliberate overfitting clarify existing experiments rather than establish revised settings or reruns.

E4.justification: V3 adds checks of stage-2 learning and generalization and sensitivity of overlap estimates to entity-parsing rules. It removes v2 Table 9's Mistral familiar-fact analysis. Existing mixing-length, mixing-ratio, mixing-source, probing, MMLU, and multi-stage analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages across three runs and retain the same three-seed standard-deviation plots in Appendix B.1, Figures 6–7. No new repeated-run counts, uncertainty-reporting practices, confidence intervals, or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: Retained table values and empirical plots are unchanged. V3 adds parameter-expansion averages of 57.8, 82.4, and 83.4 for KVR, PopQA, and TriviaQA in Table 4, stage-2 training/test results in Tables 6–7, and approximately 0.1% overlap under stricter parsing. V2's Mistral familiar-fact results in Table 9 are removed.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 corrects the displayed loss difference and stage-2 gradient evaluation point and introduces Proposition 1 with explicit first-order assumptions and a sufficient-condition claim. Appendix A's derivations are otherwise retained. The new condition does not explicitly account for the initial-loss difference or changed stage-1 gradient appearing in that appendix.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: defining continual memorization, identifying severe factoid forgetting and replay's limitations, proposing REMIX, and associating successful retention with earlier and more distributed knowledge storage. The additional evidence does not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix B.11 explicitly acknowledges uncontrolled differences between task types and exceptions involving GSM8K and WebQA. B.2 explains the intentional overfitting regime and its implications for test performance. B.10 explains why entity co-occurrence can overestimate overlap in factual relations.

D1.justification: V3 newly states that all training datasets use 2,000 examples and that non-factoid training deliberately overfits. It describes the LoRA comparator's random parameter selection without enforced separation between stages and specifies stricter entity tags. Existing learning rates, batch sizes, stopping rules, prompt examples, and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds Hu et al.'s LoRA and von Oswald et al.'s hypernetwork work in connection with the parameter-expansion comparison. The broader research positioning remains stable. Several other reference changes update publication information for already cited works rather than introduce new research.

P1.justification: V3 edits grammar and motivation in the abstract and introduction, expands the mathematical exposition, and adds appendix subsections for stage-2 performance and interpretive caveats. The main section sequence and overall narrative remain intact; there is no wholesale textual reorganization.

P2.justification: The two-column main text becomes a single-column journal layout with a new title block and headers. Figure 1 is substantially redrawn, Table 1 combines its previously stacked panels, Table 4 expands, two tables are added, and the Mistral familiar-fact table is removed. Figures and tables are extensively repositioned, although the other eleven figure graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: The added comparator and stage-2 learning/generalization checks modestly strengthen empirical scrutiny, while Appendix B.11 improves interpretation by acknowledging confounding factors and exceptions. These gains are tempered by the loss of Mistral familiar-fact evidence and Proposition 1's insufficiently justified sufficiency claim relative to Appendix A. The core method and headline results remain unchanged.
